notes: Owner-account compromise, not a fork PR. The push replaced the signed merge of
PR #267 with an unsigned twin carrying scripts/preinstall.js -- byte-identical
to the mevn-cli loader (sha256 61412c99..af100), which is what ties the two
repos to one operator. The author timestamp is the maintainer's habitual +0800,
so timezone drift is 0 here too.
Unlike mevn-cli the timestamp is NOT cloned from the parent, so the
parent-timestamp-clone signal is silent on this repo. What separates the twin
from the commit it replaced is the absent GPG signature -- which sift does not
c26b0568 was the branch head when hutning first recorded the incident on
2026-08-29; a68d2c9b replaced it in a later rewrite. Both carry the loader and
both report the same author timestamp, so the rewrite preserved the backdate

malicious_head.role: unsigned twin of the PR #267 merge, adds scripts/preinstall.js

malicious_prior_head.role: the branch head recorded 2026-08-29, before the rewrite

benign_signed_parent.role: the maintainer's own signed merge of PR #266, one commit earlier

identity_flags_do_not_discriminate.comment: The malicious twin and the legitimate merge one commit earlier raise the identical three identity flags, because both are GitHub-UI merges. Any reading that treats these flags as detection of this incident is reading noise.

signature_is_the_discriminator.comment: Signature state separates the twin from what it replaced, is deterministic, and needs no network or key material to read as present/absent. sift's runtime layer does not look at it.

parent_timestamp_clone_scan.comment: The mevn-cli signal is silent here: this attacker did not clone the parent timestamp. The two repos need different signals despite one operator.
